Series XXIII: Pride and Progress / The Right Stuff
Series XXIII: Pride and Progress / The Right Stuff

Pride and Progress News-highlights: 1. Gay Week in Review, with Andy Humm, Darrell Yates Rist, and Jim Levin, sponsored by the Human Rights Campaign Fund 2. Short news stories 3. Discussion of the increasing activism within the gay community, ties to "civil disobedience," and how to encourage new faces to join the protest COMMERCIAL: Human Rights Campaign Fund 4. New York Times reports that Southern voters are extremely concerned with AIDS as a priority issue, discussion of how the AIDS issue will be used by politicians in the 1988 election COMMERCIAL: SF AIDS Foundation, with Jose Sarria 5. Andy Humm on the AIDS education of teenagers 6. News Watch, new study shows that the longer a person is infected with HIV, the greater their chance is of developing AIDS 7. Madison Avenue advertising firm denounce remark by Lifestyles Condoms, who stated "AIDS is a condom-marketers dream" 8. AZT renamed to Retrovir, to limit confusion in foreign countries where AZT is the name of an immuno-suppressant 9. Sacramento Union publishes profile of gay male couple for Valentine series, and receives complaints 10. Sports Report 11. Lavender Health, interview with Liz [Walker], head of Domestic Violence Services at NYC Gay and Lesbian Anti-Violence Project 12. Closing credits
The Right Stuff: 1. This Week in Gay History, with Jeff Bixby COMMERCIAL: Night of a Thousand Gowns charity drag ball 2. Show Bits with George Trahanis, review of Barbara Lea's cabaret show, "The Melody Lingers On" COMMERCIAL: Zamir Furs 3. Naming Names segment, exposing persons in the media who misrepresent gay and lesbian people, sponsored by GLAAD: John Cardinal O'Connor COMMERCIAL: "Suds" gay soap opera, created by GCN 4. Media Watch with Brandon Judell, interview with Stephen McCauley, author of "Object of My Affection" COMMERCIAL: Night of a Thousand Gowns charity drag ball 5. Third part of the interview series on the operating methods of GMHC, with playwright Larry Kramer, and a response by the executive director of GMHC, Richard Dunne, tape cuts off
